verdict.rationale: ADK documents running agents on your own infrastructure: `adk run` and `adk web` run locally, `adk deploy docker` packages an agent for a local Docker container, and the docs say containerized agents can run in any container environment, including offline with no Google Cloud connection. The docs also describe adapters for locally running models. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of self-hosted deployments, and explicit evidence in the pack of the open-source license terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: This is a good option if you prefer to run offline or disconnected, or otherwise in a system that has no connection to Google Cloud.
You can manually package your Agent into a container image and then run it in any environment that supports container images.

Deploying the Agent Locally with Docker Container:

adk deploy docker --with_ui <agent-folder>
we provide adapters that let you connect with many other models and model providers, including locally running models.
